newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-RECORD GATES IN FRENCH TOP FLIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RECORD GATES IN FRENCH TOP FLIGHT.

text.p: France began their World Cup season by breaking the record for first division attendances on the first weekend of league action.
The match average of 20,488 at nine games was the first time the 20,000 mark has been passed, according to National Football League statistics published in Tuesday's L'Equipe.
The previous best was an average 19,258 in the ninth round of the 1992-93 championship.
The figure is the more remarkable considering France's major football grounds are undergoing preparation for the 1998 World Cup finals and large sections are closed.
Marseille, whose Velodrome ground has been halved in capacity by the World Cup work, packed in 23,317 against Le Havre on Saturday.
The Velodrome will be able to hold about 40,000 by the time of the World Cup draw there in December, while its capacity is being boosted to 60,000 for the finals.
Paris St Germain had the weekend's biggest crowd of 31,478 at the Parc des Princes, also a World Cup ground, for their match with promoted Chateauroux.

It also helped that clubs who traditionally draw the bigger crowds were at home. For example, Bordeaux hosted and beat champions Monaco in front of 28,339 on Friday -- Monaco average less than 6,000 for home league games.
The French first division has attracted a million more fans in the last 10 years, increasing from 4.2 million in the 1987-88 season to 5.3 million last term.
But France still lags behind the other members of Europe's big five leagues.
The average attendance last season in the German Bundesliga was 30,820, according to the figures. Italy numbered 29,775, England 28,434, Spain 23,804 and France a meagre 14,202.
